facts.raw_span: A 22-year-old woman presented for evaluation of malaligned teeth
all permanent teeth had erupted except the third molars in both arches and the lower left lateral incisor
mild spacing between the lower left central incisor and the canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion with crowding in the maxillary anterior region
no history of prior dental extractions
an unerupted lower left lateral incisor with an associated well-defined radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, which appeared to obstruct the eruption path of the tooth

all permanent teeth had erupted except the third molars in both arches and the lower left lateral incisor
mild spacing between the lower left central incisor and the canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion with crowding in the maxillary anterior region
no history of prior dental extractions
an unerupted lower left lateral incisor with an associated well-defined radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, which appeared to obstruct the eruption path of the tooth

concepts.why: The presence of a well-defined radiopaque lesion with a thin radiolucent halo obstructing the eruption path of the lower left lateral incisor is consistent with a mandibular odontogenic keratocyst.
The unerupted lower left lateral incisor with an associated radiopaque lesion could be related to a dens in dente, which is a developmental anomaly that can cause tooth impaction.
The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted lower left lateral incisor could be a compound odontoma, which is a type of odontogenic tumor that can cause tooth impaction.
The presence of a well-defined radiopaque lesion with a thin radiolucent halo obstructing the eruption path of the lower left lateral incisor is consistent with an adenomatoid odontogenic tumor.
The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted lower left lateral incisor could be a central odontogenic fibroma, which is a type of odontogenic tumor that can cause tooth impaction.

rationales.F06: The presence of an unerupted tooth with a radiopaque lesion is more commonly associated with odontogenic keratocyst and adenomatoid odontogenic tumor.
rationales.F07: The radiolucent halo surrounding the radiopaque lesion is characteristic of odontogenic keratocyst and adenomatoid odontogenic tumor, making them more likely diagnoses.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an unerupted tooth with a well-defined radiopaque lesion surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, obstructing the eruption path, is highly suggestive of an Adenomatoid Odontogenic Tumor, which is known to be associated with unerupted teeth and has a characteristic radiographic appearance.
